what: Two runs of `versionless migrate` over one already-ingested create-react-app tree, with the lane, install and build stages enabled. The first declares no peer-resolution policy and refuses by name; the second declares it and reaches a built lane. Nothing was hand-authored for this application: the lane's vite.config.ts and its rewritten package.json were both generated by the flow.

host.networkUsed: the npm registry, by the install stage, on both runs

clockRule: Single-run wall clock around the whole command, on one host. It is not a distribution and it is not comparable to the fleet dry run's per-stage medians.

runs.label: policy-not-declared

refusal.message: Install: npm refused the lane closure with ERESOLVE — a peer dependency conflict between the application's own era pins and the build toolchain the lane now declares. Declare --allow-peer-conflicts to install through it, which is a decision about what the lane's closure may be, or change what the lane declares. This flow does not take that decision on an operator's behalf.

runs.note: The lane was composed before the install stage ran, so this run also wrote the generated configuration and the rewritten manifest. What it did not do was decide, on the operator's behalf, that a peer conflict between a 2020 application closure and a current build toolchain is acceptable.

whatThisClosesFromSpikeC: C4 — 'the lane's package.json still declares react-scripts ^3.4.1 with no Vite configuration'. The lane now declares vite, pathe and ufo, its build script is `vite build`, and react-scripts is removed. Each dropped script is named as an unhandled finding rather than left as a command that cannot run.

C3 — the two npm decisions are declared flags with refusing defaults: --allow-remote-tarballs and --allow-install-scripts / --skip-install-scripts. Neither fired on this application, because its lockfile carries no non-registry tarball and no install script; both are checked from the lockfile before a registry is contacted.

A third policy of the same kind, measured here rather than inherited from the spike: a current build toolchain declared beside an era application's own pins fails npm peer resolution outright. It is now --allow-peer-conflicts, with the same refusing default.
notEstablished: A completed build is not a browser proof, a parity reading, or a witness pass. Nothing here establishes that the built lane behaves as the application did on its era toolchain, and no capability, coverage or matrix artifact was regenerated by these runs.

This is one application on one host. The install and build stages were exercised on a create-react-app tree whose lockfile needed neither the remote-tarball allowance nor the install-script allowance, so neither of those two policies was exercised against a real registry refusal here.

`closure: resolve` means npm resolved rather than replayed, because the lane manifest declares a build toolchain the recorded lockfile predates. The application's own pins still come from the lockfile; what was newly resolved is not a pin this repository recorded.

The generated configuration resolves the frozen adapter from this workspace by relative path, exactly as the fixture configurations do. The lane is buildable by this pipeline in this checkout; nothing here establishes that it builds anywhere else, and making it resolve a published @versionless/react is a packaging decision this slice did not take.
The configuration digest is a function of the specifier this host resolved the frozen adapter by, so it is a record of this run rather than a portable digest. The manifest digest is portable.
`installedPackages` counts directories in the lane's installed closure. It is not a licence reading, a provenance reading, or a vulnerability reading.
Machine seconds are single-run wall clock around the whole command on one host, including the registry install. They are not a distribution.
